verses.verse:
प्रवाहितोऽल्प बद्धश्च मुक्तश्चेति त्रिधानिलाः।
बंशादि निर्मिते वाद्ये नादस्योत्पत्तिहेतवः।६४।
verses.text: Pravāhita (flowing), alpabaddha (slightly confined) and mukta (free): air is of these three kinds, and these are the causes of the production of sound in an instrument made of bamboo and the like.

commentary.text: Whatever metal the bānsurī may be made of, the nāda (musical sound) in it arises only from air. Here air is of three kinds. The first is pravāhita (flowing): the air that flows from the player's mouth as breath through a very narrow passage and is confined on all sides. The second is (alpabaddha, slightly confined): the air that fills the inside of the bānsurī. And the third is (mukta, free): the air through which the sound is able to reach the listeners' ears. Seen this way, living beings too fall into these same three classes: 1 animals, 2 humans, 3 gods. But to see the whole world as a bānsurī, I would have to reach the level of a bānsurī player. Now we write the features and kinds of the most confined air.
